name: kvprefixes
description: The reserved-prefix write rule, per shim-writable prefix. Carried because the shim-writable allowlist is the one guard each engine enforces from its own copy of a list — the worker from `rove-reserved`, the replay prelude from a fragment generated off it — and those copies drifted once (rove#499: `_export/` was writable in prod and refused in replay). This case is what executes the pairing at runtime; the build-time assert in epilogue.zig only proves the two lists agree, not that a handler writing one of those prefixes actually replays. The `hidden` world carries the read half of the same question: the engine-only namespaces (`_usage/`, `_keys/`, …) are INVISIBLE to a handler, not refused — the rule that lets their writers stay engine writes with no activation and no log record. It also pins the refill: a page-sized run of hidden rows must not truncate a customer's scan. The `config` world pins the `_config/` resolution: a handler names the deployed path and the engine resolves it under the deployment asking, so code and config switch together (rove#726).
